touches.text: A ticket's code is a tool or machine; its life is data. All of its state is on disk, so anyone can instantiate it to talk to it, and any dialog is written to the relevant part of the ticket as it happens. To cross a gate the ticket asks that gate to queue it, sending only its fileref: devices/codemother/0/machines/<inspector>/queueme <fileref>. The gate instantiates the ticket from that fileref on its own side. A ticket instance then processes the pass or fail: on a pass it goes on to the next step, alerting the probes watching the gate (3.3.4.2); on a fail it asks design to queue it, the same way. Self-queuing is the abstract ticket's (3.3.2), so every kind inherits it and no caller queues a ticket on its behalf (Akien, same day: "that could be in the class, rather than the instance :) self queuing"). WHY: Akien, 2026-11-10: "now it has to send it's fileref over to the thing that will process it, and a new code instance created over there even tho it's the same thing... because that's good encapsulation. :)"

VERBS: status queries only (show, get), and crossing, the notice a ticket sends as it moves, which keeps the register. It answers no gate and moves no ticket. A ticket that would cross a gate asks that gate itself for an inspection, and either receives a pass or sends itself back to design (3.3.4). WHY: Akien, 2026-11-10: "why would the harbor master's bus face answer anything other than a status query. if anything (ticket) is going to try and cross a gate it's the ticket that asks that gate for an inspection. and the ticket either recieves a pass or it sends itself back to design." Measured the same day: the bus face also answers `clear` (fires clearance.py and moves a boat) and `watch` (sends a ticket to FIXME), and both leave. COMMANDS: cairn codemother harbor_master -> "652 boats (570 open, 82 in port)".

VERBS: activate, charter, deposit, drain, feedback, question, sealed (plus get and show). Moving a ticket across its workflow is the ticket's own act; CodeMother's gates only answer it (3.3.4). Each chart stage (orient through validate) and the verdict is a gate machine that answers queueme <fileref>; the ticket class queues itself to each in turn (3.3.4.3), so there is no chart or verdict verb, and `cross` leaves with the harbor's `clear` (9.4.1.5). WHY: Akien, 2026-11-10, Q#81 ("should CodeMother answer a `chart` verb ... and a `verdict` verb?"): "yes, Q#81 closes on that", that being each stage and the verdict a gate with queueme, queued by the ticket class.

COMMANDS: cairn codemother cast | cross | question | rehearse | tickets | whatsnext | seed | show dashboard; the inspectors' own shortcuts (determinism, edges, probescan, cleanup, feedbackmap) in her bin/.

conflicts.ticket_says: CodeMother declares no 'cross' verb and loses 'cross' command; the ticket's decision D5 removes 'cross' from CodeMotherDevice and deletes _handle_cross
conflicts.why: Outline 9.6 explicitly states 'so there is no chart or verdict verb, and `cross` leaves with the harbor's `clear`' — establishing that cross should not exist as a CodeMother verb. But outline 9.7's COMMANDS section lists 'cairn codemother cast | cross | question | rehearse | tickets | whatsnext | seed | show dashboard', including cross. The ticket removes cross from the implementation (correctly matching 9.6), but outline 9.7 still lists it in the commands, directly contradicting 9.6's stated intention that cross departs.
